policyHelp.tieredMeaning: “Daily: 7” keeps daily recovery points from the latest 7 days that contain backups. A day without backups does not count. Further rules add older recovery points; archives already selected do not count again.
policyHelp.tieredExample: You back up each morning and evening. With “Daily: 7” and all other rules set to 0, the evening backup remains for each of the latest 7 backup days. The morning backups may be deleted. An hourly rule or time window can keep them as well.
policyHelp.tieredDeletion: After backup, prune deletes matching archives that no active rule keeps. The values do not specify a fixed total count. Smaller values can remove many older archives at once.
policyHelp.lastMeaning: Only the archive order matters: the newest X remain, whether they were created on the same day or in different weeks.
policyHelp.lastExample: Value 3: out of 10 archives, the 3 newest remain and the 7 older ones are deleted by prune. If only 2 archives exist, both remain. The next backup already counts towards the selected limit.
policyHelp.lastDeletion: The limit applies at the next prune, including existing archives: with 100 archives and value 3, 97 may be deleted. Hourly, daily and other time rules are not active here.
policyHelp.allMeaning: Keep all existing and future archives. Automatic cleanup through prune is skipped; manual prune is also blocked for this job.
policyHelp.allExample: 10 archives become 11 with the next backup. None of the existing archives is deleted because of its age. Allow enough free storage for this.
policyHelp.allDeletion: Administrators can still explicitly delete individual archives. Compact reclaims already unused space; it does not remove retained archives. Repository checks continue.
policyHelp.withinMeaning: “7 days” means the past 7 × 24 hours, counted backwards from the time prune runs. Every archive in this window remains, including several on the same day. “14 hours” works the same way. 0 disables the window.
policyHelp.withinExample: Prune starts on Sunday at 15:00. “7 days” keeps every archive since the previous Sunday at 15:00. Adding “Daily: 7” keeps up to 7 further daily recovery points.
policyHelp.withinDeletion: Older archives are kept only by the other active rules. A time window therefore requires at least one rule such as “Daily: 1”. This prevents a long backup gap alone from making every archive eligible for deletion.
policyHelp.safetyText: At least one count rule must be active. The application rejects empty rules but does not limit the proportion of archives a valid rule may delete.
policyHelp.scope: Automatic and manual prune apply only to this job’s current archive prefix. Archives with previous prefixes remain in addition.
policyHelp.markersMeaning: A marker is a file with a name you choose. Its contents do not matter. If Borg finds that file in a source folder, it skips the entire folder, its subfolders and the marker itself. Names are case-sensitive.
policyHelp.markersExample: Enter .nobackup and create /mnt/user/data/cache/.nobackup. The folder /mnt/user/data/cache is then excluded. Other folders under /mnt/user/data are unaffected by this rule.
policyHelp.markersDeletion: Source files are not deleted. Exclusions apply to new backups and do not modify existing archives. Markers supplement the excluded paths and the uploaded exclusion file.
policyHelp.fileTitle: An exclusion file for this job
policyHelp.fileMeaning: Upload a UTF-8 text file containing Borg exclusion patterns (up to 64 KiB). The job stores its own copy. Changes to the original file on your computer take effect only after you upload it again and save the job.
policyHelp.fileExample: A line containing fm:*.tmp excludes matching temporary files. Borg ignores blank lines and comment lines starting with #. These rules supplement the other exclusions.
policyHelp.fileDeletion: The file is included in job exports and can be replaced or removed. No source files are deleted. After making changes, use a test job to check that the archive contains all required data.

mariadb.title: MariaDB database backup
mariadb.purpose: Exports databases selected in the database profile, including tables, data, views, routines, triggers and events.
mariadb.prerequisites: A running Docker container with mariadb and mariadb-dump, suitable database permissions and InnoDB base tables only. Avoid schema changes during export.
mariadb.configuration: Configure container, credentials, database selection and dump storage in Settings > Database backups. Do not assign this helper as a Pre/Post script.
mariadb.behavior: Borg Backup UI controls checks, export, gzip compression and retention. Failures prevent incomplete dumps from being archived. Global users and grants are not exported; updates may replace edits to this helper.

postgresql.title: PostgreSQL database backup
postgresql.purpose: Exports selected databases in pg_restore custom format and optionally global roles and tablespaces.
postgresql.prerequisites: A running Docker container with psql, pg_dump and pg_restore; globals additionally require pg_dumpall. The database account needs the necessary read permissions.
postgresql.configuration: Select container, credentials, databases and optional global objects in the database profile. Configure dump storage, timeout and retention there as well.
postgresql.behavior: The plugin gzip-compresses output and requires successful export before archiving. Role password hashes are omitted. Databases and global objects do not share a common snapshot. Updates may replace this helper.

source.title: Check source directory
source.purpose: Before backup, checks that the expected filesystem is mounted and an identity marker identifies the intended source directory.
source.prerequisites: The mount must already exist. A regular readable marker file of at most 256 bytes is required in the source directory; a symlink marker is rejected.
source.configuration: Set MOUNT_PATH, SOURCE_PATH, MARKER_NAME and EXPECTED_ID. Then set CONFIGURED to yes, save and assign as Pre. Suggested timeout: 30 seconds.
source.behavior: A missing mount, source outside the mount or mismatched identity blocks backup. The script does not mount storage or change source files.

space.title: Check free space
space.purpose: Checks a minimum free-space threshold on an already mounted local dump or staging filesystem before backup.
space.prerequisites: An existing mount and host tools mountpoint, df and awk. This check neither reserves space nor estimates backup size.
space.configuration: Set MOUNT_PATH and MIN_FREE_GIB, set CONFIGURED to yes and assign your copy as Pre. Suggested timeout: 30 seconds.
space.behavior: Insufficient space, a missing mount or unreadable capacity blocks backup. Remote quotas and later filesystem usage are not checked.

wake.title: Wake a server with Wake-on-LAN
wake.purpose: Sends a Wake-on-LAN packet when the target TCP port is unavailable, then waits for that port to become reachable.
wake.prerequisites: Python 3 on the host, Wake-on-LAN enabled on the target and a network that permits IPv4 broadcast. Port readiness does not verify authentication or share availability.
wake.configuration: Set MAC_ADDRESS, BROADCAST_IP, SERVER_IP, SERVER_PORT and WAIT_SECONDS; set CONFIGURED to yes and assign as Pre. Choose a timeout above WAIT_SECONDS; suggested value: 150 seconds.
wake.behavior: An already reachable port skips the wake packet. Timeout or network failure blocks backup. This script does not shut down the server after the job.

webhook.title: Send job result to a webhook
webhook.purpose: Posts job ID and the pre-Post result as JSON to your own HTTPS receiver. This is not a provider-specific notification adapter.
webhook.prerequisites: curl and Python 3 plus a private curl configuration with exactly one HTTPS URL and optional authentication headers. The file must belong to the executing user with mode 0600.
webhook.configuration: Set CURL_CONFIG to the protected file, set CONFIGURED=yes and assign as Post with “Also on failure, skip or cancellation”. Suggested timeout: 30 seconds.
webhook.behavior: Only HTTP 2xx counts as success; no automatic retries. Delivery failure fails Post and the overall job. The result describes the state before Post, not the final job status.
